newsitem.title: USA: Greyhound, Amtrak to develop new routes.
newsitem.headline: Greyhound, Amtrak to develop new routes.

text.p: Greyhound Lines Inc. and Amtrak said Thursday they agreed to develop new routes so customers can make seamless connections between bus and train.

"We are able to use existing Greyhound schedules to bring more cities into the Amtrak and Greyhound systems by making changes as small as providing Greyhound stops at rail passenger stations," Amtrak Chief Executive Officer Thomas Downs said.

Some of the cities involved have not had direct Amtrak rail service for years, such as Louisville, Ky., and Macon, Ga., the companies said. Other schedules serviced routes where Amtrak trains did not run daily, such as between Chicago, Indianapolis and Cincinnati.

Among the bus services with new connections to Amtrak effective Nov. 10 were Cincinnati to Indianapolis and Chicago; Cincinnati to Columbus and Cleveland; Macon to Atlanta; Louisville to Indianapolis and Chicago; Laredo to San Antonio, Texas, and Orlando to Melbourne and Cocoa, Fla.

In addition to these cities, Amtrak and Greyhound also planned to exchange passengers in Barstow, Calif., Battle Creek, Mich., Bellingham, Wash., Boston, Chico, Calif., Ft. Lauderdale, Fla., Harrisburg, Pa., Hartford, Conn., Holland, Mich., Houston, Kalamazoo, Mich., Kirkwood, Mo., Modesto, Calif., New Haven and New London, Conn., Newark, N.J., Oceanside, Calif., Oxnard, Calif., Pontiac, Mich., Royal Oak, Mich., Santa Ana, Calif., Spokane and Dalles, Ore.
